geo.label: tariff shock, Fed on hold
parts: Macro Stance

Growth is slowing faster than the headline data show, and inflation is not giving the Fed room. AP reported that Americans’ view of their financial futures has slumped to a 12-year low [[n12183]], and Reuters put the tariff-driven fall in consumer confidence at a four-year low [[n12257]]. Hot February inflation data sent stocks lower on March 28 [[n12561]], and a wire report says US consumers stayed cautious as inflation ticked higher [[n12660]]. Forbes is already flagging stagflation warning signs [[n13060]]. The IMF sees a slowing economy without a recession call [[n12951]], and the CBO projects US deficits rising over 30 years as growth slows [[n12930]]. The market is pricing a stagflation mix that the central bank cannot cut its way out of.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.89% and the 10Y at 4.27% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-28). The 10Y−2Y spread is +38 bps. Over 20 observations the 2Y fell 10 bps while the 10Y rose 3 bps, so the spread widened 13 bps; over five observations the 2Y is down 5 bps and the 10Y is up 2 bps. The 3M bill is at 4.33%, leaving the 10Y−3M spread at -6 bps, and the 30Y is at 4.64%. The curve is positively sloped and the 20-observation move is steepening (10Y up, 2Y down/flat). Equities are being repriced against that backdrop: the S&P 500 closed at 5,580.94, down 6.27% over 20 sessions, the Nasdaq 100 is down 7.68% over 20 sessions and down 2.61% in the prior session, and the VIX at 21.65 rose 15.84% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The dollar index stands at 104.04 index points, down 3.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
New / Most Important

The signal that matters is that inflation is refusing to fall. The hot February inflation read [[n12561]] and the 2.5% headline PCE reading CoinGape reported [[n12544]] keep the easing timeline on hold. Bostic expects only one FOMC rate cut this year [[n12107]], and Musalem says the risk that inflation stalls above 2% or moves higher has increased [[n12858]]. The political overlay is new: Trump is zeroing in on the Fed and setting up a possible fight with Powell [[n12808]], and he has said he hopes the Fed will lower rates [[n12726]]. That combination is why the 2Y has rallied only modestly while the 10Y stays higher.
Playbook ✓

Stay defensive into the next data. Trim cyclical US exposure (autos, homebuilders, discretionary retail): KB Home has already cut its outlook as consumer confidence fell [[n12111]]. Own gold as the hedge against a Fed that cannot cut, and keep index puts while the VIX holds above 20. The front end is where duration is worth adding, since the 2Y has fallen over 20 observations. Change the call if the Nasdaq 100 reclaims its 20-session reference of 20,884.41 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28) and the 10Y stops rising.

geo.label: cuts priced, autos exposed
parts: Macro Stance

Euro-area policy is leaning toward easing while the trade shock lands on manufacturers. French and Spanish inflation undershot, which Bloomberg read as backing the ECB’s cuts [[n3763]], and the ECB has warned banks about liquidity risk from geopolitical shocks [[n3699]]. The euro fell to a three-week low as Trump imposed auto tariffs [[n3611]], and France says it hopes to avoid a trade war but is ready to respond [[n3815]]. The euro is still stronger against the dollar over 20 sessions, at 1.0801, up 3.90% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
Credit & Inflation

Consumers are the ECB’s problem: Schnabel says households may be put off by an inflation misperception [[n3703]]. Bank consolidation is moving with supervisory approval, since UniCredit received ECB approval to take over Banco BPM [[n3794]] and Santander and BBVA are seeking favourable capital treatment from the ECB [[n3736]]. Equities are weaker than the currency: the STOXX Europe 600 closed at 542.10, down 2.71% over 20 sessions, and the Euro Stoxx 50 at 5,331.40, down 2.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
New / Most Important

Autos are the transmission channel. The European auto sector slammed the 25% tariffs and called for retaliation [[n3081]], and Porsche and Mercedes face a $3.7B hit from US auto levies [[n3199]]. Germany is urging a strong response to Trump’s auto tariffs [[n3713]]. The auto proxy has taken the hardest hit: the iShares STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles & Parts ETF closed at 49.05 euros, down 8.74% over 20 sessions, with BMW down 9.49% and Volkswagen preferred shares down 6.86% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
Playbook ✓

Underweight German and French autos until the tariff path is settled, and hedge through the sector ETF rather than a single stock. Own euro-area defence where capacity is being added, with Rheinmetall as the reference: Moody’s upgraded it to Baa1 with a stable outlook [[n10317]], and its CEO is visiting VW plants as defence companies look to expand [[n10374]]. Change the call if the STOXX 600 reclaims its 20-session reference of 557.19 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28) while the ECB’s cut expectations stay in place.

geo.label: stimulus support vs trade shock
parts: Macro Stance

Beijing is signalling support while the export machine runs into tariff politics. A vice premier pledged more policy support and said the economy started 2025 well [[n1546]], and the economy tsar invited the EU trade chief to jointly resist tariff threats [[n1551]]. Xi is working the CEO audience too, urging global executives to protect trade as Trump’s tariffs loom [[n1634]]. The policy message is growth-supportive; the trade message is defensive. The currency is steady rather than weak: USD/CNY at 7.2633 is up only 0.22% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), so the yuan is not the channel through which the trade shock is being absorbed.
PMIs & Activity

Activity is being read through trade and tech demand rather than through the surveys. The Financial Times reports China’s export boom has sparked a record number of trade challenges [[n1724]], and Reuters says the trade war feels much worse this time for China and US companies [[n1726]]. Demand for compute is strong: China’s H3C warned of an Nvidia AI chip shortage amid surging demand [[n1648]]. The view holds while factory readings stay above the 50 line and export orders keep their momentum; a slide below 50 would confirm that stimulus is not yet reaching manufacturing. Chip demand is the cleanest read on activity right now, and it runs against the tariff story rather than with it.
Credit Impulse

Bank capital is the credit story, not a new credit boom. Nikkei Asia reports bad loans rose at Chinese state banks ahead of a $69bn capital injection [[n1625]], and Global Times reports four state-owned banks will bring in the Finance Ministry as a strategic investor to reinforce capital adequacy [[n1723]]. Reuters says the top Chinese banks’ profits stagnated and margins shrank as the economy weighed [[n1673]], while South China Morning Post reports 2024 profits rose and non-performing loans dipped even as margins stayed thin [[n1643]]. The impulse is defensive: state capital supports lending capacity, but lending data have to confirm the turn before the credit cycle does. Lending capacity, not loan demand, is what the recapitalisation changes first, so the banks’ capital position comes before the loan growth figures.
Property

Property is splitting. South China Morning Post reports Shanghai’s luxury property market is thriving while the mass housing segment is deteriorating [[n1739]]. That split is the policy test: support that reaches mass housing would be a real turn, while support that only lifts the top end is a tilt, not a repair. Watch the mass segment and the mainland developers that finance it, not the luxury headline.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Trade is where policy is being made. Xi’s charm offensive comes days before Trump unveils fresh tariffs, CNN reports [[n1638]], and Japan, South Korea and China agreed to strengthen trade ties as US tariffs loom [[n1740]]. The Japan Times frames the same meeting as three countries vowing to strengthen ties [[n1732]]. Beijing is building alliances around trade, which keeps the policy response aimed at the external shock rather than at domestic consumption. The public message to foreign partners is stability and the message at home is support for growth; the two only conflict if tariffs widen beyond the sectors now under pressure.
Markets & Flows

The Hang Seng closed at 23,426.60 index points, down 0.65% in the prior session and up 2.12% over 20 sessions. The Shanghai Composite at 3,351.31 index points is up 0.92% over 20 sessions, the CSI 300 ETF (ASHR) at 26.62 dollars is up 0.19% over 20 sessions, KWEB at 35.04 dollars rose 3.27% over 20 sessions, and USD/CNY at 7.2633 is up 0.22% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Reuters reports Chinese investors poured record funds into Hong Kong stocks in the first quarter [[n1642]], while South China Morning Post reports BlackRock sold its last Shanghai asset at a discount amid China retreat [[n1651]]. The AI leg is Alibaba: CNBC puts its rally at $100 billion [[n1525]]. Hong Kong is ahead of the mainland on the 20-session view, with the Hang Seng up 2.12% against the Shanghai Composite’s 0.92% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
New / Most Important

The most important development is that the state is putting capital into the banks. The Finance Ministry becoming a strategic investor in four state-owned banks [[n1723]] is the signal to watch: it lets lending capacity expand without a new stimulus headline, which is why the credit impulse reads as repair rather than boom.
Playbook ✓

Own Hong Kong and US-listed China internet exposure only as a trade into policy headlines, using KWEB as the vehicle. Avoid mainland banks on credit growth until lending data confirm the recapitalisation, and keep yuan exposure small while USD/CNY sits at 7.2633. Size positions small until export orders show whether trade frictions are spreading. ⚠ Divergence: the Shanghai Composite is up 0.92% over 20 sessions while the S&P 500 is down 6.27% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), so the mainland market is not following the US sell-off.

geo.label: hawkish BOJ, tariff exposure
parts: Macro Stance

The BOJ is the swing factor. Yen buyers are pricing a hawkish central bank [[n5827]], and core inflation at 3% in February kept rate-hike bets alive [[n5674]]. The 10-year yield hit a 16-and-a-half-year high [[n5735]], and the Sumitomo Mitsui markets head sees the BOJ rate at a 30-year high [[n5752]]. The BOJ’s newest board member avoided signalling the timing of the next hike [[n5792]], which leaves the market to make the call.
Activity & Currency

USD/JPY closed at 150.8470, up 0.25% in the prior session, up 1.51% over five sessions and up 0.56% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The Nikkei 225 closed at 37,120.33 index points, down 1.80% in the prior session and down 2.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Tariff exposure is the drag: Toyota went from bullish on Trump to the tariff threats [[n5715]], and Prime Minister Ishiba says Japan is putting all options on the table [[n5806]]. Core inflation in Tokyo accelerated but stayed above the BOJ target [[n5794]]. A weaker yen helps exporters’ margins while the tariff bill rises.
New / Most Important

Markets are bracing for a cut to the BOJ’s super-long bond buying [[n5844]]. That is the signal that matters in JGBs, because it changes the price of the long end rather than the policy rate. Japan will also give crypto assets legal status as financial products, Nikkei says [[n5843]].
Playbook ✓

Hedge yen exposure in the exporters rather than shorting the currency outright, favour the domestic banks that gain from a higher rate path, and treat the super-long end as the risk. Change the call if USD/JPY falls back below its 20-session reference of 150.0120 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28) and the 10-year yield stops rising.

geo.label: election call, soft-landing test
parts: Macro Stance

Australia’s cycle goes to the ballot box. The prime minister has called a general election for May 3 amid cost-of-living pressure and tariff worries [[n0467]]. The RBA question is open: ABC asks whether another rate cut is coming [[n0545]], and AFR argues three changes are still needed to realise the central bank’s potential [[n0541]]. The budget papers say the economy is on track for a soft landing [[n0419]], but budget forecasts may be blown away by the trade war [[n0398]].
Demand & Financing

AUD/USD closed at 0.6302, up 0.23% in the prior session and up 1.11% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The S&P/ASX 200 closed at 7,982.00 index points, up 0.64% over five sessions but down 2.33% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The AFR says super funds’ global push is threatening the Aussie dollar [[n0436]], CNBC reports the dollar is unmoored as traders are unsure on tariffs [[n0408]], and AFR reports that wealthy suburbs are turning to buyers’ markets as house prices slump [[n0390]].
New / Most Important

Rio Tinto will lower the iron content of its flagship Pilbara Blend fines as ore quality weakens, S&P Global reports [[n0515]]. That is a pricing and volume signal for the iron-ore leg of the index, and it matters more to the ASX 200 than the RBA debate does.
Playbook ✓

Own the miners with copper and gold exposure rather than the banks until the election. Hedge some AUD exposure into the vote, since the currency has already gained 1.11% over 20 sessions and the super-fund outflow story is a headwind. Change the call if the S&P/ASX 200 reclaims its 20-session reference of 8,172.40 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).

geo.label: rate-hold risk, defence bid
parts: Macro Stance

The rate path could stay on hold. TVN24 reports there is a risk the RPP will not change rates at all this year [[n6403]], and Glapiński says more lending needs a change to the bank tax [[n6488]]. The NBP president is also drawing criticism for promoting gold purchases, which Money.pl calls another communication error in an opinion piece [[n6444]]. The labour market is holding: BIEC sees stabilisation with unemployment at 5% [[n6542]], and Parkiet says unemployment has not risen and for now will not [[n6409]]. High inflation is mainly regulatory and fiscal in origin, according to a trade-portal piece [[n6462]]. The zloty has firmed against the dollar, with USD/PLN down 3.25% over 20 sessions, which takes some pressure off imported prices (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
Markets

USD/PLN closed at 3.8732, down 3.25% over 20 sessions from 4.0035, and EUR/PLN at 4.1833 is up 0.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The iShares MSCI Poland ETF (EPOL) closed at 28.43 dollars, up 12.46% over 20 sessions, and the Beta ETF WIG20TR tracker at 52.26 zloty is up 6.65% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Leadership has rotated to energy and rate-sensitive names: PGE at 8.57 zloty is up 20.35% over 20 sessions, PKO Bank Polski at 76.70 zloty is up 11.00%, Orlen at 69.04 zloty is up 10.11%, and mBank at 835.40 zloty is up 12.86% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Reuters reports the Warsaw Stock Exchange’s core profit rose on record revenue growth [[n5931]]. The laggards are consumer and coal names: Dino Polska is down 7.99% over 20 sessions and JSW is down 11.37% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Rate-sensitive banks and utilities are the cleanest test of the hold: a flat rate path keeps the margin story intact while the bank-tax debate runs.
Fiscal & Politics

The budget fight is about the banks. Wnp.pl asks whether rising bank profits should carry extra taxes [[n6418]], and a second commentary puts the excess-profit question directly [[n6548]]. Glapiński’s call for a bank-tax change is the fiscal link to lending [[n6488]]. The finance minister has set the timetable for the tax-free allowance [[n6493]], which is the household-side fiscal signal. Politics is in campaign mode: a left-wing presidential candidate is calling for cuts to state funding for the church [[n5919]].
Corporate & Sectors

Banks are the rate-sensitive core of the index: PKO and mBank have risen 11% and 13% over 20 sessions even as the bank-tax debate builds. Orlen agreed a pay deal with raises and cash bonuses for staff [[n6573]], and has sent a notice to prosecutors over its purchase of Ruch shares after an audit, wnp.pl reports [[n6568]]. KGHM’s board is preparing a multi-year investment plan [[n6584]], while the company says small modular reactors are not yet profitable [[n6492]]. CD Projekt is under fire, and Parkiet asks where the share price goes next [[n6480]]; the next Witcher is due in 2027 at the earliest [[n6457]]. PZU’s holding-company restructuring is the insurer’s agenda [[n6570]]. KGHM’s investment plan is the company-level signal to watch.
Geopolitics & Security

NATO’s secretary general told Warsaw that a Russian attack on Poland would meet a full-force response [[n5942]], and NATO’s chief said the response would be devastating [[n5960]]. Poland plans to use EU Covid recovery funds for defence and security spending [[n5951]], and the government has approved financing for its first nuclear plant, which still awaits EU approval [[n5947]]. Interia Wydarzenia reports Poland is arming at a record pace [[n6440]]. A security chief’s warning that supplies would last a week or two drew attention [[n5966]], and the government has suspended the right of migrants to apply for asylum [[n5968]]. Defence spending is the policy line that connects the budget debate to the equity rally, with NATO commitments and EU funds the two sources the government is leaning on.
New / Most Important

The signal that matters is the rate path. A hold for the year, the risk TVN24 flags [[n6403]], would turn Polish equities into a yield-and-defence story rather than a rate-cut story. Glapiński’s push for a bank-tax change to get lending moving [[n6488]] is the policy decision to watch, because it ties bank profits to credit growth.
Playbook ✓

Own the energy and defence names on their own catalysts (Orlen’s pay deal, KGHM’s plan, the NATO spending push) and keep the banks as a tactical trade against the bank-tax debate. Keep PLN exposure small against the euro while EUR/PLN is up 0.53% over 20 sessions. ⚠ Divergence: the banks are rallying as hard as the index (PKO is up 11.00% over 20 sessions) even as the bank-tax debate intensifies, which is the signal that contradicts the rate-hold story.
Narrative

Technology is down 8.49% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), and the semiconductor index is down 10.11% over the same stretch. The consensus says AI demand is intact; the fear is the AI-bubble argument, and CoreWeave’s co-founder says the company does not understand the AI bubble fears [[n4288]]. Micron started shipping HBM3E for AI servers in partnership with Nvidia [[n3190]], which is the demand proof the group needs.
Reported

Pure Storage’s full-year EPS missed expectations [[n3228]], SentinelOne’s EPS missed [[n3205]], and Verint missed on full-year numbers [[n3212]]. Couchbase’s EPS beat [[n3076]], and Sapiens’ full-year EPS missed [[n3230]]: four misses against one beat across the five reports.
EPS Upside Watch

Couchbase is the one beat, so the bar is lower for software names with AI-data demand, and Micron’s HBM3E volumes are the upside into the next quarter. Apple is quietly ditching Broadcom’s Wi-Fi chips, Moomoo reports [[n3250]], which is a risk for Broadcom into its next report; Broadcom is down 15.20% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The hardware orders are the swing factor for the next beat, and the software misses set a lower bar for the rest.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that the AI capex chain rises with the chip index. Oracle is reportedly the latest tech giant hit by DOGE cuts [[n3196]], which shows the government-software leg of cloud spend is not the safe harbour it was assumed to be.
Narrative

Communication services are down 6.14% over 20 sessions, with Alphabet down 9.37% and Meta down 13.69% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The narrative is ad-cycle caution under tariff pressure, and the platforms are being judged on AI spending rather than on engagement. Advertising-linked revenue is the sensitivity to watch, since that is where tariff-driven caution shows up first.
Reported

The sector’s hard datapoint is Disney’s Snow White opening, which faltered at the box office and saw the stock slip on Friday, TradingView reports [[n7131]]. The BBC reports Disney faces a US investigation over DEI practices [[n10541]].
EPS Upside Watch

Meta is the bulls’ name: a Motley Fool headline argues there are three reasons to buy the stock [[n6996]]. The upside case rests on estimate revisions still to come, after a 13.69% fall over 20 sessions.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Quant signals still flag Alphabet as a buy [[n4019]], yet the stock is down 9.37% over 20 sessions. The convention is that quant buy signals lead the price; here the price has already moved against them.
Narrative

Financials are down 5.69% over 20 sessions and regional banks are down 9.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The narrative is recession odds: a Deutsche markets survey puts the probability of a recession approaching 50% [[n12718]], and CNBC’s survey of CFOs says a recession is coming before the end of 2025 [[n12799]].
Reported
Jefferies’ stock sank as the firm attributed soft results to geopolitics, Investopedia reports [[n3104]]. An analyst at Wells Fargo lowered Truist’s price target to $50 from $52 [[n3231]].
EPS Upside Watch

Fee-heavy names are set up: Bloomberg reports Bank of America boosted its 2025 muni sales forecast to $580 billion [[n13005]], and CNBC reports JPMorgan and BlackRock want to privatise more of retail’s stock and bond money as markets stay volatile [[n13088]]. Those are fee lines that hold up in a sell-off. Trading and capital-markets revenue is the swing line if volatility stays high.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Bank of America says the Trump put is alive and well [[n12961]], even though markets have given up on it. The convention is that a policy put backs the banks; the bank view depends on a policy reversal that has not been delivered yet.
Narrative

Energy is up 1.57% over 20 sessions while WTI crude, at 69.36 dollars a barrel, is down 0.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The supply story is OPEC+: oil fell on an OPEC+ output hike and Trump’s tariffs [[n10724]]. The risk story is sanctions: Trump floated fresh sanctions on Russian oil [[n5385]] and threatened tariffs on Russian oil if Moscow blocks a Ukraine deal [[n5356]]. The US majors are the less-levered version of the same trade, with volume growth the missing piece.
Reported
CNOOC’s net profit surged on record output [[n3071]], and PetroChina reported record 2024 net income on higher production [[n3247]]. Both are volume stories, not price stories.
EPS Upside Watch
The upside is volume: record output carried both results. Exxon’s billion-dollar growth plan [[n4191]] is the Western version of the same argument, and it needs a price that holds.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that OPEC+ output hikes cap prices. The counter-argument is the sanctions threat, and The Guardian says it could hit China and India [[n5395]]. If buyers are penalised, supply tightens while the OPEC+ headline says it loosens.
Narrative

Industrials are down 4.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The narrative is trade cost in aerospace: the Airbus chief says the trade war will get worse before it gets better [[n10642]], while lessors keep ordering, with BOC Aviation buying 50 Boeing 737 MAX jets [[n10654]] and BOC Aviation also set to buy 120 Airbus and Boeing jets to grow its fleet [[n10708]].
Reported
AAR Corp’s Q3 profit beat estimates and its shares rose premarket, Stocktwits reports [[n3218]]. KKR and Japan’s state-backed JIC are taking Topcon private for $2.31 billion [[n3226]].
EPS Upside Watch

AAR is the template: a beat that carries into a premarket lift. Lessor orders [[n10708]] support backlog for aerospace suppliers, and defence names are reading the same demand signal, with AFR reporting that defence stocks are rocketing [[n10111]]. Backlog conversion is the number to watch, because the lessor orders only help if the factories deliver.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that aerospace leaders are the defensive core of industrials. Yahoo Finance frames GE Aerospace as surging in 2025 [[n7227]], yet GE Aerospace is down 3.43% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28): the premium is not in the price.
Narrative

Discretionary is down 8.76% over 20 sessions, with Nike down 20.32% and Lululemon down 19.84% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Lululemon shares dropped 15% after the CEO said inflation and economic concerns are weighing on spending [[n3109]], and Walmart’s CEO says customers are exhibiting stressed behaviours [[n12402]]. The Walmart and Lululemon readings point the same way: the consumer is trading down and cutting discretionary spend.
Reported

Dillard’s full-year results beat expectations [[n3236]], and NEXT’s revenues beat expectations while EPS lagged [[n3192]]. Barron’s reports Olive Garden’s parent stock is soaring and asks what Darden needs now [[n7240]].
EPS Upside Watch

PVH’s fourth-quarter report is previewed [[n0602]], which sets up the apparel names. Dillard’s beat suggests department-store margins are holding, so the set-up favours the names that already beat the consumer slowdown.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that Tesla is a cyclical name in the sector. Tesla is up 5.97% over five sessions even as the sector is down 8.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), so the stock is being bought on politics rather than on the car cycle.
Narrative

Staples are the defensive refuge, but XLP is down 3.21% over 20 sessions and up 1.36% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Walmart is the test: a Yahoo Finance analyst piece frames it as the best consumer staples stock to buy [[n12653]], while Walmart’s CEO says customers are exhibiting stressed behaviours [[n12402]]. The defensive bid is real but selective.

Costco’s Kirkland Signature is driving growth and profits, CNBC reports [[n3221]], which is the private-label read across the staples group.

Private label and trade-down favour grocers and warehouse clubs into the next quarter, and Costco’s store-brand momentum is the set-up [[n3221]]. Staples with wholesale pricing have the most room to beat if trade-down accelerates.

The convention is that staples are immune to tariffs. Walmart’s CEO flagged customers stressed enough to take $22 billion off the company’s valuation [[n12402]], which says the defensive group carries consumer risk too.
Narrative

Healthcare is a policy story. HHS cuts reach the FDA, which will lose 3,500 jobs [[n12656]], and FDA staff are struggling to meet product review deadlines after DOGE layoffs, Reuters reports [[n12442]]. Biotech is down 4.86% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).

Milestone Pharmaceuticals’ stock plunged 60% after the FDA declined to approve its nasal spray, and Stocktwits notes retail is still positive [[n7201]].
EPS Upside Watch

Novo Nordisk is set up as a value case: Quartz reports Wegovy is getting cheaper [[n7124]], and Seeking Alpha calls the stock a buying opportunity [[n10721]]. Novo is down 23.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), so the earnings bar is low. The regulatory and staffing noise is the swing factor for the group, and the FDA staffing story is the one to watch.

Gold miners (GDX) are up 14.73% over 20 sessions and Freeport-McMoRan is up 4.09% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Copper here is an asset tied to grid and data-centre capex. Copper and gold give the group a real bid even as the rest of the sector lags.
Reported
Gold Road Resources hit a record high after spurning Gold Fields’ bid, Reuters reports [[n12665]]. Rio Tinto will lower the iron content of its Pilbara Blend fines as ore quality weakens [[n0515]].

Gold miners are set up on price: the cost base is fixed while the metal runs, so the earnings beat is the cleanest read on the metal. Gold futures are up 8.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
⚡ Breaking Convention

XLB is down 4.18% over 20 sessions even as copper and gold miners rise. The convention that metals lift materials breaks at the basket level, so the group is a stock-picker’s sector rather than a metal proxy.
Narrative

Real estate is down 4.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Mortgage rates are expected to stay higher for longer [[n12366]], and mortgage payments are rising to an all-time high [[n12477]]. The rate path is the constraint, not the demand. The housing read is the most rate-sensitive in the sector, so the next data prints will test how far mortgage costs have squeezed demand.
Reported
KB Home cut its outlook as consumer confidence fell [[n12111]]. Bank of America’s mortgage applications jumped 80% in Q1, an executive says [[n12425]].

Homebuilders have the least room to surprise on the upside. The mortgage applications rebound [[n12425]] is demand, but the cost of the mortgage caps the sales price and the margin.

Mortgage applications jumped 80% in Q1 [[n12425]] while mortgage payments are at an all-time high [[n12477]]. That cuts against the convention that housing waits for lower rates before demand returns.
Narrative

Utilities are being rerated on power demand. The WSJ says economic growth now depends on electricity, not oil [[n12942]], and CNBC reports the nuclear companies leading the race to build advanced small reactors in the US [[n7225]]. XLU is down 1.57% over 20 sessions, with Duke up 1.63% and Southern up 1.49% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
Reported

The sector’s reads come from its power names: Vistra is down 10.93% over 20 sessions and Constellation Energy is down 18.02% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), even as the power-demand story is the strongest in the window.
EPS Upside Watch

Power-demand names set up for upward revisions if data-centre demand holds. Johor’s data-centre boom is the Asian proof point, though South China Morning Post asks who will create the jobs [[n12619]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that AI power demand equals a utility bid. Vistra and Constellation are down 10.93% and 18.02% over 20 sessions while Duke and Southern are up over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), so the power bid is not lifting every name in the group.
Narrative

European autos are down 8.74% over 20 sessions on the 25% tariff, with BMW down 9.49% and Mercedes down 6.73% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Europe’s auto sector slammed the tariffs and called for retaliation [[n3081]]. The European auto move is about the US tariff bill, not about the European demand cycle.
Reported
The reported number is a tariff bill rather than an earnings miss: Porsche and Mercedes face a $3.7B hit from US auto levies, Automotive News reports [[n3199]].
EPS Upside Watch
Stellantis is reopening a US car factory, a project that will take two years [[n10754]]. The upside is in the US footprint for 2026 estimates, not in the European earnings base.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that tariffs on imported cars help domestic makers. Bloomberg reports Elon Musk is one of the few winners from Trump’s car tariffs [[n3080]], and Reuters says the auto tariffs will hurt Trump’s working-class supporters [[n5396]]. The tariff bill lands on the buyer as well as the importer.
Narrative

Semiconductors are down 9.51% over 20 sessions for the SOXX ETF, and the SOX index is down 10.11% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The narrative is split between shortage and capex caution: China’s H3C warns of an Nvidia AI chip shortage amid surging demand [[n1648]], while TSMC, Intel and other top chipmakers are slowing Japan and Malaysia expansions, Nikkei Asia reports [[n5835]].
Reported

Micron started shipping HBM3E for AI servers in partnership with Nvidia [[n3190]]. Qualcomm has taken its antitrust fight with Arm to regulators in the US, Europe and Korea, Stocktwits reports [[n6939]].
EPS Upside Watch

Micron’s HBM3E ramp is the upside into the next report. ASML is down 4.87% over 20 sessions on a stock already marked down (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), and Nvidia’s May 15 date [[n7102]] is the calendar anchor for the group.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The convention is that the shortage narrative lifts every chip name. ASML is down 4.87% and TSMC is down 8.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), so the shortage argument is not lifting the whole group. The read-across to the capex names is the test: if the expansions slow, the shortage argument loses its support.

earnings_pattern.title: Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
parts: Rewarded

Beats with a lift in the outlook were paid. NEXT jumped 8% after it cleared the £1 billion profit line [[n3116]], and Bloomberg reports NEXT surged after it raised its forecast, defying a weak UK economy [[n3726]]. AAR Corp’s Q3 profit beat estimates and its shares rose premarket [[n3218]], and Barron’s reports Olive Garden’s parent stock is soaring [[n7240]]. Couchbase beat on EPS [[n3076]], the one software beat in the window. The reward goes to beats that come with a forward view, not to the beat alone.
Punished

Misses without a raised outlook were not forgiven. Lululemon shares dropped 15% as the CEO flagged inflation and economic concerns weighing on spending [[n3109]]. Pure Storage’s full-year EPS missed [[n3228]], SentinelOne missed [[n3205]], and Verint missed [[n3212]]. 3D Systems tumbled after a bigger-than-expected Q4 loss [[n7110]], and Katapult beat on revenue but its losses exceeded Wall Street projections [[n7198]].
Pattern

Raised forecasts were paid: NEXT surged after it raised its forecast [[n3726]], while 3D Systems tumbled after a bigger-than-expected loss [[n7110]]. NEXT beat on revenues but EPS lagged [[n3192]], and the shares still rose on the raised forecast, so the reaction follows guidance more than the headline number. The forward view decides the tone when revenue beats, which is why the NEXT print matters more than its headline sales figure.
Attention into EPS

The set-ups are visible. PVH’s fourth-quarter report is previewed [[n0602]], Micron’s HBM3E shipments [[n3190]] set the chip bar, and Nvidia’s May 15 date [[n7102]] is the largest calendar item in the group. AppLovin took a third short seller’s attack, which drove the shares down 20% [[n3060]], and the company has hired a law firm to investigate the allegations [[n7116]].
Playbook

Own the beat-and-raise names into their next print, avoid revenue-only beats with a soft EPS line, and keep AI-linked exposure sized for the Nvidia read rather than adding shorts. Change the call if guidance is cut and the stock reaction turns positive, which would show the market has moved past the EPS line.

underowned.title: Europe outside the defence trade
parts: Attention Gap

Make Europe Great Again trades are gaining traction, Reuters reports [[n3820]], which suggests the reallocation away from US exposure is still early and not yet crowded. Foreign investors are selling US stocks, and Barron’s says tariffs are the problem [[n4199]]. The STOXX Europe 600 is down 2.71% over 20 sessions while the DAX is down only 0.40% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), so the group is not yet a consensus position.
Exposure & Risk

Name the instruments: the Europe ETF (VGK) at 70.98 dollars is up 1.11% over 20 sessions, and the Euro Stoxx 50 ETF (FEZ) at 55.01 dollars is up 1.76% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The risk is that the trade war lands on Europe first: France says it is ready to respond [[n3815]].
Trigger to Watch

A tariff settlement that spares European autos would turn the theme into a consensus trade quickly. Watch EUR/USD, up 3.90% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), for the first sign of a reversal.

underowned.title: Uranium and enrichment
parts: Attention Gap

The attention is on small reactors rather than fuel: CNBC reports the nuclear companies leading the race to build advanced small reactors [[n7225]]. The uranium boom has fizzled as Ukraine ceasefire talks build [[n8209]], and Kiplinger is pitching uranium ETFs as a way to play the nuclear theme [[n8864]].
Exposure & Risk

URA at 23.10 dollars is down 6.85% over 20 sessions, Centrus Energy (LEU) at 66.25 dollars is down 26.98% over the same stretch, and Cameco (CCJ) at 41.83 dollars is down 5.02% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Enrichment is the bottleneck, so single-name risk is high.
Trigger to Watch

A ceasefire that drains the geopolitical premium pushes the group lower; enrichment-capacity contracts push it higher. Watch LEU for a move back above its 20-session reference of 90.73 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).

underowned.title: Dollar hedging and ex-US assets
parts: Attention Gap

Dollar dominance is under pressure, CNBC reports [[n4276]], and analysts say de-dollarisation could speed up with US isolationist policies [[n4184]]. Barclays argues the dollar has not priced in the impact of tariffs [[n4320]].
Exposure & Risk

The DXY is at 104.04 index points, down 3.32% over 20 sessions, while EUR/USD is up 3.90% and USD/JPY is up 0.56% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The Japan ETF (EWJ) at 69.22 dollars is up 1.10% over 20 sessions, a simple ETF route to the same view.
Trigger to Watch
A close back above 107.61 index points, the 20-session reference from February 28, would say the dollar is recovering and the hedge is wrong. A hot PCE-type print keeps the dollar bid.

underowned.title: Copper as an asset, not a growth gauge
parts: Attention Gap

Copper hit a record high on tariff bets and halted shipments [[n12811]], and Chase Bank reports copper prices have reached an all-time high [[n9628]]. The metal is being traded as tariff plumbing and grid capex, which is why it is under-discussed next to the AI names.
Exposure & Risk

Copper is at 5.11 dollars a pound, up 13.25% over 20 sessions. The copper miners ETF (COPX) at 40.01 dollars is up 4.68%, and Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) at 38.42 dollars is up 4.09% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The risk is a tariff premium that unwinds.
Trigger to Watch

A reversal in the tariff premium would cut the trade back toward its pre-tariff level. A data-centre or grid order that names copper in volume would turn it into a capex asset, and the miners are the cleanest way to hold that view.

crypto.title: Crypto & Digital Assets — the bounce is still a range
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at $82,334.52, down 0.32% in the prior session, down 5.87% over five sessions and up 4.84% over 20 sessions against 78,532.00 on March 10 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-30). Ether closed at $1,806.22, down 12.65% over five sessions and down 2.95% over 20 sessions, while Solana at $124.64 is up 5.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-30). Crypto equities are more volatile than the coins: Strategy is up 13.30% over 20 sessions, Coinbase is down 19.33% and the bitcoin ETF IBIT is down 0.71% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). CoinDesk reports bitcoin dropped to $82K as traders fled risk assets amid macro worries [[n2309]].
New / Most Important

Reuters reports Japan will give crypto assets legal status as financial products, Nikkei says [[n5843]], a structural bid that will take time to show in prices. The near-term driver is macro: Yahoo Finance reports Bitcoin, Ethereum and Dogecoin plunged on the day [[n2283]], which shows how the coins are trading with the risk complex. Ether lags the rest of the group, so the bitcoin bounce is not yet a broad crypto recovery.
Playbook

Hold core bitcoin exposure inside the range, with 78,532.00 from March 10 as the line to respect: a close below it turns the bounce into a failed one. Avoid levered miners, where Cipher Mining is down 43.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Ether is the weak link: buy it only after a move back above its 20-session reference of 1,861.15 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-30). Watch Strategy’s shares as the equity proxy for bitcoin, since they moved more than the coin over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).

flows.title: Capital Flows & Liquidity Framework — central banks set the floor, the crowd sets the tape
parts: Global Liquidity

Markets are bracing for a cut to the BOJ’s super-long bond buying [[n5844]], which is a liquidity withdrawal at the long end. The ECB has warned banks about liquidity risk from geopolitical shocks [[n3699]], and Deutsche Bank says Fed backstop fears could threaten the dollar [[n12943]]. Bloomberg reports the Fed has been urged to mull a hedge-fund bailout facility for basis trades [[n4195]], which shows where the stress sits. In China the state is supplying the cushion: a $69bn capital injection is ahead for the state banks [[n1625]]. A cut to the BOJ’s super-long buying would tighten liquidity at the long end while the White House presses the Fed to cut [[n12726]], and those cross-currents are what the market is trying to price.
Rates & Dollar

DXY is at 104.04 index points, down 3.32% over 20 sessions. TLT is at 90.14 dollars, up 1.38% in the prior session and down 2.48% over 20 sessions, while HYG at 78.80 dollars is down 1.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). CNBC reports the dollar is hovering ahead of PCE and the tariff onslaught [[n4294]], and Reuters says the dollar slipped on growth fears before the next tariff announcement [[n4295]]. Yahoo Finance reports US bond investors are weighing convexity risk in the recent Treasury yield decline [[n12813]]. A weaker dollar eases funding for the rest of the world and supports the non-US equities that are still underowned, which is why the dollar leg matters beyond currency traders.
Credit Check

Credit is holding up better than equities. HYG is down 1.66% over 20 sessions against the S&P 500’s 6.27% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), and the investment-grade LQD at 108.48 dollars is down 1.03% over the same stretch. Bloomberg reports Bank of America raised its 2025 muni sales forecast to $580 billion [[n13005]], and Goldman and BNP see a Korean convertible boom as shorting resumes [[n12864]]. In Bloomberg’s Credit Weekly, Khosla sees one of the best opportunities in a decade [[n0599]]. High-yield is the early warning: HYG holding up better than the S&P 500 says the drawdown has not yet reached credit, and a break in high-yield would say it has.
Equity & Fund Flows

Everyday investors are buying the dip at near-record levels as tariffs spook Wall Street, Business Insider reports [[n7008]], and a Yahoo Finance commentary asks why investors are buying the dip [[n3234]]. Foreign investors are selling US stocks, Barron’s reports [[n4199]]. Chinese investors poured record funds into Hong Kong in the first quarter [[n1642]], and BlackRock sold its last Shanghai asset at a discount [[n1651]]. UBS joined Wall Street firms in cutting its S&P 500 target to below 6500 [[n4325]]. Reddit’s 50% plunge is failing to attract dip buyers as growth slows [[n3201]], which is a selective crowd in one line. The flows read is two-sided: retail is buying the dip while foreign investors are selling, and the mix decides whether the rebound lasts.
Portfolio Implication

Liquidity is state-led in China and central-bank-led in Japan and the euro area, and the US is the marginal risk. Keep the dollar and long-end hedges on, and treat retail dip-buying as a sentiment risk rather than a floor. Change the call if credit spreads tighten while the S&P 500 recovers part of its 20-session loss, since that would mean credit is not confirming the equity sell-off. Hedges are cheapest when the tape looks firm, so the flow picture argues for buying protection on rallies rather than after the next leg lower.

anticipatory.title: Tariff escalation and retaliation
parts: What Is Priced

Trump is due to unveil fresh tariffs, CNN reports, with Xi’s charm offensive running days before the announcement [[n1638]]. Canada says it will respond to Trump’s auto tariffs with its own trade actions [[n5054]], and Europe’s auto sector has called for retaliation [[n3081]]. The S&P 500 is down 6.27% over 20 sessions and the Nasdaq 100 is down 7.68% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), so part of the escalation is already in the price.
Conditional Expression

If the new tariffs are broad, the trade is long gold and the dollar hedge, short the European auto proxy (down 8.74% over 20 sessions), and cautious on the US consumer. If they are narrowed or paired with talks, the trade reverses into autos and cyclicals. India and the US are making progress towards a trade deal, Reuters reports [[n5337]], which is the template for narrowing.
Risk

The risk is a retaliation cycle that hits the US consumer first: Walmart’s CEO says customers are stressed [[n12402]], and Americans’ view of their financial futures has slumped to a 12-year low [[n12183]]. Hot inflation [[n12561]] leaves the Fed unable to cushion the hit, which is the stagflation path.

anticipatory.title: Fed: one cut, sticky inflation
parts: What Is Priced

Bostic only expects one FOMC cut this year [[n12107]], and Musalem warns inflation could stall above 2% or move higher [[n12858]]. Trump hopes the Fed will lower rates [[n12726]], and The Hill reports he is zeroing in on the Fed with a possible fight with Powell [[n12808]]. The 2Y closed at 3.89% and the 10Y at 4.27% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-28), so the front end is pricing a slow path.
Conditional Expression

A cut priced back in makes the 2Y the long and the 10Y the short, a steepener in line with the 20-observation move. A cut pushed further out reverses it: the 2Y sells off relative to the 10Y and the trade becomes a flattener. Either way, the steepening direction is the one to respect until the front end changes its message.
Risk

The risk is a bear steepener: Fed-independence worries push long yields higher even as the front end rallies on cut bets. That is the tail where gold and term premia both rise, and the White House pressure on the Fed makes it more likely.

anticipatory.title: Iran, Russia and the oil supply
parts: What Is Priced

Oil is priced for two outcomes at once. Iran has rejected direct negotiations with the US in response to Trump’s letter [[n5365]], and Trump threatened bombing if Iran does not make a nuclear deal [[n5391]]. Trump floated fresh sanctions on Russian oil [[n5385]], while oil fell on an OPEC+ output hike and Trump’s tariffs [[n10724]]. WTI is at 69.36 dollars, down 0.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
Conditional Expression

If sanctions on Russian buyers bite, buy front-month crude and the energy sector (XLE is up 1.57% over 20 sessions). If the OPEC+ hike is confirmed and Iran talks stall, the supply premium fades and energy becomes a trading range. Brent at 73.63 dollars, up 0.61% over 20 sessions, is the cross-check (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
Risk
The knock-on is that The Guardian reports the Russian oil sanctions threat could hit China and India [[n5395]], an Asian demand risk that offsets the supply premium.

anticipatory.title: AI capex into May
parts: What Is Priced

Nvidia has a May 15 date that Business Insider flags as key [[n7102]]. The market is pricing a shortage and a slowdown at once: H3C warns of an Nvidia AI chip shortage [[n1648]], while the CoreWeave co-founder says the company does not understand the AI bubble fears [[n4288]]. The SOX index is down 10.11% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28).
Conditional Expression

If the Nvidia read confirms capex, buy the pullback in Micron. If capex guidance softens, the thin-margin, high-beta names reprice first: Super Micro is down 17.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), and CoreWeave is the newest test.
Risk

The risk is the AI-bubble argument becoming consensus. Futurism says AI’s biggest test is turning into a catastrophe as CoreWeave flounders [[n10639]], and the thesis fails if demand bends before capex does.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — the May 15 capex check
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Business Insider flags May 15 as the date to watch for Nvidia’s stock [[n7102]]. Moody’s lifted Nvidia’s rating to Aa2 with a positive outlook [[n3000]], and H3C warns of a chip shortage amid surging demand [[n1648]]. The thesis is that the AI demand signal is intact and the stock has been marked down with the group rather than on its own numbers.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NVDA closed at 109.67 dollars, down 6.82% over five sessions and down 12.21% over 20 sessions from 124.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The hurdle is the 124.92 reference, and the risk is the AI-bubble argument gaining ground into the date.
Trade Expression
Buy a call spread into the Nvidia read with the long strike near the 124.92 reference, invalidated by a close below 100 dollars.

catalysts.title: $MU — HBM3E ships with Nvidia
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Micron shipped HBM3E for AI servers in partnership with Nvidia [[n3190]], and a Motley Fool headline calls it a stock that will soar over the next three years [[n3200]]. The thesis is the memory tier of the AI build, where volume shipments come before the price.
Price Hurdle & Risk

MU closed at 88.44 dollars, down 6.63% over five sessions and down 5.54% over 20 sessions from 93.63 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The hurdle is the 93.63 reference; the risk is that the group’s drawdown, with SOXX down 9.51% over 20 sessions, deepens first.
Trade Expression
Buy the shares on a close above 93.63, invalidated by a close below 88.44, the last close.

catalysts.title: $RHM — defence re-rating in Europe
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Moody’s upgraded Rheinmetall to Baa1 with a stable outlook [[n10317]], and its CEO visited a VW plant as defence companies look to expand [[n10374]]. Reuters reports ‘Make Europe Great Again’ trades are gaining traction [[n3820]]. The thesis is spending and balance-sheet capacity, with the rerating already well advanced.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Rheinmetall closed at 1,310.00 euros, down 2.96% in the prior session and up 30.15% over 20 sessions from 1,006.50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). A Seeking Alpha headline says the shares have gained 2,000% and have nowhere to go but down [[n10590]], which is the crowd-risk view.
Trade Expression
Own the cash equity on pullbacks toward 1,006.50 euros, invalidated by a close below that level.

catalysts.title: $APP — short sellers keep coming
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

AppLovin shares plunged 20% after a third short seller slammed its ad technology [[n3060]]. Bloomberg reports the company has hired a law firm to investigate short-seller allegations [[n7116]], and Morningstar calls it another short-seller report [[n3167]]. The thesis is that the pressure persists until the company answers the allegations with numbers.
Price Hurdle & Risk

APP closed at 272.38 dollars, down 13.26% over five sessions and down 16.38% over 20 sessions from 325.74 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The hurdle is the 325.74 reference; the risk is a squeeze if the company answers the allegations convincingly.
Trade Expression
Buy a put spread below 272.38, invalidated by a close above 325.74.

catalysts.title: $RDDT — dip buyers stay away
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Bloomberg reports Reddit’s 50% plunge is failing to entice dip buyers as growth slows [[n3201]], and Yahoo Finance asks why the stock is down that day [[n6984]]. The thesis is that the growth slowdown is the catalyst and the dip buyers are not stepping in.
Price Hurdle & Risk

RDDT closed at 107.71 dollars, down 6.91% over five sessions and down 33.42% over 20 sessions from 161.78 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The hurdle is the 161.78 reference; the risk is a short-covering rally on any single positive data point.
Trade Expression
Bear put spread below 107.71, invalidated by a close above 161.78.

catalysts.title: $NVO — the cheaper Wegovy
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Quartz’s pharma roundup reports Wegovy is getting cheaper [[n7124]], and Seeking Alpha calls Novo a buying opportunity [[n10721]] while asking which is the better bargain, Novo or Eli Lilly [[n3238]]. The thesis is that price cuts compress near-term numbers, though the stock already reflects a good deal of that.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NVO closed at 69.30 dollars, down 9.84% over five sessions and down 23.55% over 20 sessions from 90.65 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The hurdle is the 90.65 reference; the risk is another price-cut headline.
Trade Expression
Pair long Eli Lilly against short Novo Nordisk, invalidated if the price cut is matched by volume growth.

retail_intro: The dominant popular-narrative trade is the Musk dip in Tesla, anchored on Cathie Wood’s $2,600 target [[n6779]], and it rhymes with the 2020 Tesla run, the 2021 GameStop squeeze and the 1999 infrastructure trade.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — Musk is back, buy the dip
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The crowd’s story is that Musk is back in charge and the stock is being punished for politics and a weak economy, not for the car business. Fortune reports a Tesla analyst saying Musk is ‘back in charge’ after a surprise all-hands meeting, with investors rewarding the stock [[n6848]]. Cathie Wood sticks with Tesla and predicts $2,600 a share [[n6779]], the number retail anchors on. Stocktwits had the stock extending a winning streak to five days, with retail more bullish [[n6874]]. It feels obvious because the dip looks like a discount on a company everyone already owns.
What Is Driving It

Tesla closed at 263.55 dollars, down 3.51% in the prior session, up 5.97% over five sessions and down 10.05% over 20 sessions from 292.98 on February 28 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). The Nasdaq 100 fell 2.61% in the prior session and 7.68% over 20 sessions, the VIX rose 15.84% in the prior session to 21.65, and the 10Y is at 4.27% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-28). The catalysts are politics and demand: Fortune reports Cathie Wood says the stock’s problem is not just Musk’s politics but a bad economy hitting demand [[n6849]]. Bloomberg reports Musk is one of the few winners from Trump’s car tariffs [[n3080]], a line the bulls will repeat. Musk has also said Tesla is not immune to tariffs [[n1649]], which is the bear’s half of the same argument.
The Social Signal

Attention looks like a Stocktwits headline about a five-day winning streak [[n6874]] and a TradingView headline about a retail buying frenzy [[n6769]]. Yahoo Finance reports TSLA has become a meme stock, according to a top investor [[n7093]], and the Motley Fool keeps the $2,600 call in headlines [[n7230]]. The protest side is loud: Protests hit Tesla dealerships across the world, The Guardian reports [[n7242]], and a Tesla Takedown day of action against DOGE cuts reached the Bay Area [[n10664]]. Musk’s reaction to Tim Walz mocking the stock’s slide is going viral [[n3239]]. Retail reads the viral row as a rallying cry, not a warning.
Historical Analog

The closest mechanical analogue is the dot-com pattern. MarketWatch’s headline says the dot-com bubble peaked 25 years ago [[n12717]], and Yahoo Finance’s anniversary piece asks which stocks investors wish they had bought [[n6810]]. The mechanics are general: the first wave buys the story; the second wave buys the stock because not owning the story starts to look like a mistake; and dips get bought until the buyers run out. Retail is in the second wave, which arrived after the Musk narrative was already a headline everywhere. The useful lesson is about timing: the second wave is the one that buys the top, which makes the analogue a warning about the crowd rather than a forecast for the stock.
Smart Money View

Support comes from named analysts and the bulls. Cathie Wood sticks with Tesla and predicts $2,600 [[n6779]], and Fortune reports a Tesla analyst reads Musk as back in charge [[n6848]]. Caution comes from Business Insider, which says Tesla has flirted with disaster before but this time feels different [[n6850]], and from a top investor, who says TSLA has become a meme stock [[n7093]]. Fortune says furious shareholders have two main options to push for change [[n7182]]. The disagreement is about pace more than direction: the bulls accept a long path to the target, while the bears argue that politics and demand block the path. Both sides agree the stock is trading on Musk.
When the Narrative Breaks

Price levels define the break: the 20-session reference close is 292.98 and the last close is 263.55, so a close below 263.55 takes the rebound off the table. The observable trigger is politics: AP reports Musk handing out $1 million payments after the Wisconsin Supreme Court declined to stop him [[n4350]], the kind of headline that moves the crowd in both directions. The instrument risk is leverage: TQQQ is down 23.47% over 20 sessions and SOXL is down 29.48% over the same stretch (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28), and leveraged funds fall faster than the stock in a sell-off. This desk’s view matches the US playbook: dip-buying into a stagflation print is the risk, not the floor.

retail.title: Gold and silver / GLD — the fear trade that keeps going
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Gold is the trade people can explain at a dinner table. When the tariff shock lands, gold hits fresh highs, Yahoo Finance UK reports [[n3768]], and MarketWatch says gold is crushing the S&P 500 [[n12770]]. Bankier.pl reports gold at a new record and analysts rushing to raise their forecasts [[n6585]]. Kitco gives silver the squeeze label [[n7085]], and the silver trust’s net asset value has reached $6 billion [[n7088]]. The crowd’s line is simple: when the stock market gets nervous, the metal is the answer.
Where It Breaks

Gold futures closed at 3,086.50 dollars an ounce, up 8.36% over 20 sessions from 2,848.50 on February 28; GLD at 284.06 dollars is up 7.90% over 20 sessions from 263.27, and silver at 34.64 dollars is up 10.97% over 20 sessions from 31.22 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). A close back below 2,848.50 would end the 20-session move. The instrument risk is silver’s volatility, and the reversal trigger is a tariff truce or Iran talks that remove the fear premium; Iran has already rejected direct negotiations [[n5365]], so the premium is still in place.

retail.title: CoreWeave / CRWV — the AI cloud IPO that would not pop
parts: Why Retail Is Here

CoreWeave is the AI story that arrived as an IPO. It priced at $40 a share, below the expected range [[n4174]], and was downsized [[n4315]]. Bloomberg says the shares whipsawed after the heavy cut to a $1.5 billion offering [[n3173]], and Reuters says it was valued at $23 billion in a muted Nasdaq debut [[n3174]]. The crowd’s logic is that Nvidia built the company into a major AI player years before helping save its IPO [[n2327]], and CNBC reports the shares closed flat at $40 after the biggest US tech IPO since 2021 [[n3195]].
Where It Breaks

The stock has a single close so far, $40.00 on March 28 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). A close below the $40 IPO price would break the flat debut and revive the AI-bubble argument that the co-founder says the company does not understand [[n4288]]. The instrument risk is that a newly listed stock has no return history to lean on, and Futurism’s headline says the AI test is turning into a catastrophe for CoreWeave [[n10639]].

retail.title: GameStop / GME — the meme stock buys bitcoin
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story is simple and the crowd repeats it: a retail favourite is turning into a bitcoin treasury. Reuters reports GameStop’s crypto pivot boosted shares of a one-time retail favourite [[n6916]], and Yahoo Finance asks whether the meme stock is back after a 15% jump on the bitcoin bet [[n6914]]. Fortune reports the stock then slid 23% after the strategy shift and the plan to buy $1.3 billion of bitcoin [[n2153]]. The hook is the meme comeback, with bitcoin as the new reason to own it.
Where It Breaks

GameStop closed at 21.73 dollars, down 1.63% in the prior session, down 12.20% over five sessions and down 13.22% over 20 sessions from 25.04 on February 28 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-28). Reuters reports shares tumbled as investors questioned the bitcoin pivot [[n7014]], and the company plans to raise $1.3 billion to buy bitcoin [[n2154]]. A close back above 25.04 would undo the 20-session drop. The instrument risk is that the stock now trades on the bitcoin price: bitcoin is down 5.87% over five sessions at $82,334.52 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-30).
